query: FeCoNi is an fcc alloy with high saturation magnetization and a low coercive field. Earlier studies examined the high-entropy alloys FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt, but both exhibited soft ferromagnetism. A qualifying high-entropy alloy must have an almost equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R. Subject to these constraints, what single intervention could produce a FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy with greater coercivity than the prior derivatives? Present one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to an appropriate FeCoNi-based baseline, defines the conditions over which it should apply, cites supporting observations from earlier work, and proposes a discriminating experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.mechanism: the addition of Cr reduces the magnetization due to antiparallel coupling of the Cr spins to the Co/Fe/Ni spins, driving the alloy toward a more magnetically anisotropic state

falsification_experiment.design: prepare FeCoNi alloys with varying amounts of Cr (0-20 at.%) and measure their coercivity and saturation magnetization
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: if the coercivity of the FeCoNi alloy with 10 at.% Cr is not at least 20% higher than that of the baseline FeCoNi alloy, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: While the AlCoFeNi high entropy alloy exhibits a single ordered B2 phase at high temperature, both the substitution of ferromagnetic Co with antiferromagnetic Cr, and lower annealing temperatures lead to a tendency for this system to decompose into a two-phase mixture of ordered B2 and disordered BCC solid solution. The length scale of this decomposition is determined by the combination of composition and annealing temperature, as demonstrated in this investigation by comparing and contrasting AlCoFeNi with the AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi alloy. The resulting phase stability has been rationalized based on solution thermodynamic predictions. Additionally, it is shown that replacement of Co by Cr in the AlCoFeNi alloy resulted in a substantial reduction in saturation magnetization and increase in coercivity. The microhardness is also strongly influenced by the composition and the length scale of B2 + BCC decomposition in these high entropy alloys.

The configurational space of alloying five or more different elements offers a huge playground to tune magnetic properties. For example, the addition of Cr to an equiatomic FeNiCo alloy which exhibits high saturation magnetization (Ms) (151 Am2/kg) and low coercivity Hc = 120.96 A/m [] significantly reduces the magnetization due to antiparallel coupling of the Cr spins to the Co/Fe/Ni spins and drives the CoCrFeNi alloy toward paramagnetism at room temperature []. Further addition of Al, Pd, or Ga promotes ferromagnetism and increases Ms from 0.5 to 13 Am2/kg, 34 Am2/kg and 38 Am2/kg and the Curie temperature to 277 K, 503 K and 703 K, respectively [,]. The enhancement was assumed to be due to the partial phase transition to a bcc phase.
